title: PRD: Optimize eval acceptance — sentinel composition, A/B decision ladder, and rollback triggers
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: This PRD defines acceptance and rollback criteria for the Optimize product evals pipeline focused on balancing sensitivity to regressions with noise-resilience. It introduces a sentinel composition approach (mix of synthetic probes, production cohorts, and adversarial checks), an A/B decision ladder for progressive rollouts, and a matrix of rollback triggers mapped to impact categories. The goal is to provide predictable, actionable signals for releases that change model family, quantization, or prompt transformations.
background: Current Optimize evals use single-threshold alerts on aggregate metrics and a small set of manual prompt checks. Recent incidents showed both missed regressions (low coverage of edge cohorts) and false positives (high sensitivity to sampling variance). We need a formalized, multi-signal acceptance contract that is prescriptive for PMs/Engineers and automates safe rollout behavior when combined signals cross defined bands.
scope: In-scope: (1) Define sentinel composition and sampling plan (synthetic + production cohorts + adversarial). (2) Specify metric families and comparison modes (absolute, relative, effect-size). (3) Define multi-signal decision ladder for A/B canaries (red/amber/green thresholds and required concurrent signals). (4) Design rollback trigger lattice and automated traffic steering actions. (5) Integration points for the console alerting and Optimize eval dashboard.
out_of_scope: In-scope excludes: re-implementing eval ingestion pipeline, model retraining workflows, and backend infra changes that are pure performance optimizations. Also excludes post-mortem tooling for incidents unrelated to eval-triggered rollbacks.
requirements_clarification: 1) Prompt cohorts must include at least 3 production-user cohorts representing high-volume, low-volume, and safety-sensitive traffic. 2) Synthetic probes will be user-owned prompt categories (10-30 prompts each) and must include expected canonical outputs for exact-match checks + soft similarity scoring. 3) Metric families: latency, response-quality composite (Q-score), hallucination-rate (precision on factual queries), instruction-following accuracy. 4) Statistical test: use bootstrap confidence intervals and Cliff's delta for effect size; require minimum N per cohort. 5) A/B windows default to 72 hours unless traffic or variance suggests longer.
scope_changes: 2026-03-12: Added 'adversarial probes' bucket after security/ML review requested more targeted safety checks. 2026-03-14: Reduced default A/B window from 7 days to 72 hours to speed feedback; added requirement to extend window when sample variance > 0.2. 2026-03-15: Clarified that rollback automation is gated behind an explicit PM/Eng approval toggle per release.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Sentinel composition defined and implemented for at least two internal product teams. 2) Dashboard shows per-cohort metrics with CIs and effect-size annotations. 3) A/B decision ladder configured: green (no action), amber (throttle + increased sampling + PM notification), red (auto-fallback or rollback depending on policy). 4) Rollback triggers: red requires >=2 high-confidence signals (e.g., cohort decline >5% absolute AND Q-score Cliff's delta >0.2) OR a single high-severity safety sentinel failure. 5) All alerts generate runbook links and a one-click rollback/traffic-shift action in the console. 6) End-to-end tests for canary lifecycle pass in CI and a staged manual canary demonstrates correct behavior.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for sentinel selection logic and threshold evaluation.
- Synthetic canary runs with injected regressions to validate alerting and rollback behavior.
- Shadow A/B run on a low-traffic product for two weeks to measure false-positive rate.
- Manual ops drill with on-call and PM to execute rollback runbook.
- Statistical validation harness verifying sample sizes, CIs, and effect-size computations.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (Week 1-2): Implement sentinel definitions and dashboard visuals for 2 pilot teams (billing and search).
Phase 2 (Week 3): Enable A/B decision ladder with amber notifications; require manual approval for red actions.
Phase 3 (Week 4): Flip 'auto-rollback' toggle for low-risk models and run one controlled auto-rollback experiment with infra rollback guardrails.
Phase 4 (Week 5+): Iterate thresholds based on pilot false-positive/false-negative rates and expand to additional teams.
monitoring_and_signals: Primary signals: per-cohort Q-score (mean + 95% CI), hallucination-rate (false positive rate on ground-truth probes), latency p95, adoption/usage drop per cohort. Secondary signals: token cost delta, error-rate. All signals surface a confidence band; automated signal fusion requires at least two concordant signals in the same severity band before red action unless a safety sentinel fails.
mitigation_playbook:
Amber: Throttle new traffic allocation to the candidate release (50% -> 20%), increase sampling on affected cohorts, notify PM/Eng with triage checklist.
Red: If auto-rollback enabled: run single-step fallback to previous model variant and re-route 100% traffic to previous stable route. If auto-rollback disabled: create high-priority incident, run manual rollback with documented comms.
Post-rollback: run regression analysis on prompt cohorts, capture root cause, and update sentinel set if needed.
